name: Yala National Park
conservation_notes: Known for one of the highest leopard densities in the world; the park closes for part of the year for conservation — confirm exact dates for the current year.
description: Sri Lanka's most visited national park, renowned for having one of the highest leopard densities in the world alongside elephants and sloth bears.
source: Sri Lanka Tourism Development Authority; Dept. of Wildlife Conservation
cost_breakdown: Entry fee (foreign visitor) ~Rs 18,000 + jeep safari hire ~Rs 22,000 (per group, shared) + guide/tracker fee ~Rs 5,000

name: Udawalawe National Park
conservation_notes: Reliable elephant sightings due to open grassland habitat; lower entry cost than Yala, popular budget-friendly wildlife option.
description: Open grassland and scrub around the Udawalawe reservoir offering reliable elephant sightings, with an on-site elephant transit home.
cost_breakdown: Entry fee (foreign visitor) ~Rs 7,000 + jeep safari hire ~Rs 9,000 (per group, shared) + guide/tracker fee ~Rs 2,000

name: Sinharaja Forest Reserve
conservation_notes: UNESCO World Heritage rainforest with high endemic biodiversity; strict guide requirements and trail restrictions apply.
description: A UNESCO World Heritage rainforest and the last major tract of primary tropical rainforest in Sri Lanka, home to high endemic biodiversity.
source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre; Forest Department
cost_breakdown: Entry/permit fee ~Rs 8,000 + mandatory guide fee (multi-day) ~Rs 12,000 + forest dept conservation fee ~Rs 2,000

name: Horton Plains National Park
conservation_notes: High-altitude cloud forest and grassland; home to World's End escarpment. Early morning entry recommended before cloud cover sets in.
description: A high-altitude cloud forest and grassland plateau home to the sheer World's End escarpment and Baker's Falls.
cost_breakdown: Entry fee (foreign visitor) ~Rs 28,000 + jeep/transport to trailhead ~Rs 5,000 + optional guide ~Rs 2,000

name: Wilpattu National Park
conservation_notes: Sri Lanka's largest national park, known for its natural sand-rimmed lakes (villus) and leopards; reopened in 2010 after a long closure during the conflict period.
description: Sri Lanka's largest national park, known for its natural sand-rimmed lakes (villus) and a strong leopard population.
cost_breakdown: Entry fee (foreign visitor) ~Rs 16,000 + jeep safari hire (longer routes) ~Rs 21,000 (per group, shared) + guide/tracker fee ~Rs 5,000

name: Minneriya National Park
best_season_detail: Jun-Sep ("The Gathering" — elephant herds at the reservoir)
conservation_notes: Famous for one of Asia's largest elephant gatherings around the Minneriya tank during the dry season.
description: Home to 'The Gathering', one of Asia's largest seasonal elephant congregations around the ancient Minneriya tank.
source: Dept. of Wildlife Conservation; Sri Lanka Tourism Development Authority
cost_breakdown: Entry fee (foreign visitor) ~Rs 14,000 + jeep safari hire ~Rs 19,000 (per group, shared) + guide/tracker fee ~Rs 5,000

name: Wasgamuwa National Park
conservation_notes: Less-visited elephant habitat, promoted as a quieter, lower-cost alternative to Minneriya/Udawalawe.
description: A quieter, lower-cost elephant habitat promoted as an alternative to the busier Minneriya and Udawalawe parks.
cost_breakdown: Entry fee (foreign visitor) ~Rs 6,000 + jeep safari hire ~Rs 8,000 (per group, shared) + guide/tracker fee ~Rs 2,000

name: Kumana National Park
conservation_notes: Adjoins Yala; internationally recognised for migratory water birds nesting in the Kumana mangrove swamp.
description: Adjoining Yala, internationally recognised for migratory water birds nesting in the Kumana mangrove swamp.
cost_breakdown: Entry fee (foreign visitor) ~Rs 15,000 + jeep safari hire (remote, longer transfer) ~Rs 20,000 (per group, shared) + guide/tracker fee ~Rs 5,000

name: Knuckles Mountain Range
conservation_notes: UNESCO World Heritage extension site (part of the Central Highlands listing); montane cloud forest with strict trail-guide requirements.
description: A UNESCO World Heritage montane cloud forest offering multi-day trekking routes through rugged, biodiverse mountain terrain.
source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre; Forest Department
cost_breakdown: Entry/permit fee ~Rs 6,000 + mandatory trekking guide fee (2-day) ~Rs 12,000 + forest dept fee ~Rs 2,000

name: Ella Rock
conservation_notes: Popular unmarked hiking trail through tea estates and forest; local guides recommended to avoid getting lost on the informal path network.
description: An unmarked hiking trail winding through tea estates and forest to a scenic viewpoint above the hill-country town of Ella.
cost_breakdown: Local guide fee (recommended, not mandatory) ~Rs 8,000 + transport/tuk to trailhead ~Rs 3,000 + incidental costs ~Rs 1,000

name: Adam's Peak (Sri Pada)
conservation_notes: Sacred mountain significant to multiple faiths; the main pilgrim route is lit and most active Dec-May, quieter and less maintained outside this season.
description: A sacred mountain significant to multiple faiths, climbed via a lit pilgrim staircase to a summit shrine and sunrise viewpoint.
cost_breakdown: Transport to base (Nallathanniya) ~Rs 6,000 + optional porter/guide ~Rs 4,000 + incidental/refreshment costs ~Rs 4,000 (no formal entry ticket)

name: Riverston (Riverstone Peak)
conservation_notes: Scenic viewpoint and hiking area within the Knuckles range, known as a cooler, less-crowded alternative to the main Knuckles trails.
description: A scenic viewpoint and hiking area within the Knuckles range, known as a cooler, less-crowded alternative to the main trails.
cost_breakdown: Local guide fee ~Rs 8,000 + jeep/transport to trailhead ~Rs 5,000 + incidental costs ~Rs 2,000

name: Sigiriya (Lion Rock)
conservation_notes: UNESCO World Heritage ancient rock fortress; visitor numbers and climbing access are managed to protect the frescoes and structure.
description: A UNESCO World Heritage 5th-century rock fortress with frescoes, mirror wall, and water gardens rising 200m above the plain.
source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre; Dept. of Archaeology
cost_breakdown: Entrance ticket (foreign visitor rate) ~Rs 42,000 + optional local guide fee ~Rs 6,000

name: Polonnaruwa Ancient City
conservation_notes: UNESCO World Heritage medieval capital; ruins are spread over a wide area, commonly explored by bicycle.
description: Sri Lanka's UNESCO-listed medieval capital, with ruins spread over a wide area commonly explored by bicycle.
source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre; Dept. of Archaeology
cost_breakdown: Entrance ticket (foreign visitor rate) ~Rs 27,000 + bicycle hire (site is spread out) ~Rs 3,000 + optional guide ~Rs 2,000

name: Anuradhapura Sacred City
conservation_notes: UNESCO World Heritage first ancient capital of Sri Lanka; includes active sacred sites, so modest dress and conduct guidelines apply.
description: Sri Lanka's UNESCO-listed first ancient capital, home to active sacred sites and centuries-old Buddhist monuments.
source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre; Dept. of Archaeology
cost_breakdown: Entrance ticket (foreign visitor, round ticket) ~Rs 20,000 + local transport/bicycle hire between sites ~Rs 3,000 + optional guide ~Rs 2,000

name: Dambulla Cave Temple
conservation_notes: UNESCO-listed cave temple complex with well-preserved murals; a lower-impact, easily-accessible cultural stop compared to open-air ruin sites.
description: A UNESCO-listed cave temple complex with well-preserved murals, offering an easily-accessible, lower-impact cultural stop.
cost_breakdown: Entrance ticket (foreign visitor rate) ~Rs 17,000 + optional local guide fee ~Rs 3,000

name: Mirissa (Whale & Dolphin Watching)
conservation_notes: Sri Lanka's best-known whale-watching hub; boat operators are subject to Sea Mammals Observation, Regulation and Control Regulations enforced by the Coast Guard — use licensed operators only.
description: Sri Lanka's best-known whale and dolphin watching hub, with boat excursions departing from a lively south-coast beach town.
source: Sri Lanka Tourism Development Authority; tourism operator guides (verify current-season dates)
cost_breakdown: Boat tour fee, licensed operator ~Rs 27,000 + optional hotel pickup/transport ~Rs 3,000

name: Rekawa Turtle Watch
best_season_detail: Year-round nesting; Nov-Apr for best weather
conservation_notes: Community-run night turtle watching under conservation-group supervision; strict rules on lighting, flash photography and touching nesting turtles.
description: A community-run night turtle watching site near Tangalle, operated under conservation-group supervision.
source: Turtle Conservation Project; Sri Lanka Tourism Development Authority
cost_breakdown: Community-run turtle watch fee/donation ~Rs 10,000 + community guide fee ~Rs 3,000 + transport to site ~Rs 2,000

name: Kalpitiya Peninsula
conservation_notes: Large resident pods of spinner dolphins and seasonal whale sightings; quieter and less commercialised than Mirissa but tours are typically more expensive.
description: A quieter dolphin and whale watching destination with large resident spinner dolphin pods, less commercialised than Mirissa.
cost_breakdown: Dolphin/whale watching boat tour, smaller group ~Rs 65,000 + hotel pickup/transport ~Rs 10,000

name: Pigeon Island National Park
conservation_notes: Marine national park with protected coral reef and reef-shark sightings; snorkelling access is regulated to limit reef damage.
description: A marine national park off Trincomalee with protected coral reef and reef-shark sightings, popular for snorkelling.
cost_breakdown: Marine park entry fee ~Rs 10,000 + boat transfer to island ~Rs 14,000 + snorkelling gear hire ~Rs 7,000 + guide/lifeguard fee ~Rs 5,000
